dam_isthmus: A narrow neck of continuous land joining larger land masses, with water on either side.
dam_draught: A drawn view or outline for identifying a coast or other geographical feature.
dam_route: A passage made by ship through particular waters.
dam_journal: A dated written record kept in sequence during a voyage.
dam_surveyor: Measure actual positions on the ground or water to plot a chart.
dam_commissioner: Person entrusted with administering a public office by commission.
dam_chair: Presiding officer of a learned society.
dam_governance: The way a community is governed.
dam_appendix: A supplement planned for the end of a volume.
dam_track: The course actually sailed, including its depiction on a chart.
dam_countryman: A person of the same country as the speaker.
dam_candour: Willingness to judge another's conduct generously.
dam_soil: The earth of a particular tract considered as the growing medium.
dam_halt: Call briefly at a port or island while voyaging.
dam_cay: A low offshore islet or key.
dam_publication: The act of issuing this printed account.
dam_curiosity: An interest in acquiring or examining knowledge.
dam_mapregion: A geographical description of a particular region.
dam_company: The people sailing together aboard a ship.
dam_traverse: An actual journey or segment of a route taken through a locality.
dam_outrigger: Dampier's more precise name for the solid lateral float of a canoe.
dam_reader: The person reading the printed voyage.
dam_dot: A single puncture-like point in a charted route.
dam_manuscript: A text written by hand, here the Spanish written source for the coastal survey.
dam_reduction: A smaller scale rendering made from a larger map or survey.
dam_reference: A direction within the text to another section or volume.
dam_station: A place from which a navigator observes and plots a feature.
dam_steer: Guide the course of a vessel.
dam_arrival: The event of reaching a particular place.
dam_term: A word used in a particular trade or branch of knowledge.
dam_solid: Wood whose inside is solid rather than hollowed out.
dam_spelling: The sequence of letters used in writing a name.
dam_logwood: The dyewood cut for trade in the Bay of Campeachy.
dam_rum: The distilled cane liquor bought in Jamaica.
dam_passenger: Person travelling aboard another's vessel without joining the crew as a seaman.
dam_privateer: A private maritime raider or a vessel engaged in such raiding, preserving the narrator's designation.
dam_canoe: A locally made narrow boat, called a canoa by Dampier; distinguished from the larger periago.
dam_periago: The vessel locally called a periago, distinguished in this account from canoas.
dam_longboat: The larger open boat carried or towed by a ship; also called the launch in this narrative.
dam_loyal_merchant: London merchant vessel bearing this name; the name is rendered for its sense.
dam_miskito: A member of the Moskito people in Dampier’s account. The term is the author's ethnonym and does not denote an insect.
dam_ashore: On or onto land in contrast to aboard ship.
dam_gulf: A wide inlet of the sea, here the Gulf of Mexico or of St Michael.
dam_venture: A risky venture undertaken in a new place.
dam_agreement: An understanding reached by members of the expedition.
dam_management: The way a captain conducts the affairs of a travelling company.
dam_exp: A journey undertaken by a company for a particular purpose.
dam_obstruction: An obstacle that interrupts the progress of a voyage.
dam_turtle: Marine turtle, as distinct from the turtle-dove and the broader tortoise term.
dam_manatee: The aquatic mammal that the narrator also calls the sea cow.
dam_chocolate: Ground cacao made up with sugar as a portable provision.
dam_water_cask: A water container made here from sections of a canoe and called a bumkin.
dam_windward: Toward the quarter from which the wind comes.
dam_leeward: On the side away from the prevailing wind.
dam_cruiser: A vessel cruising an assigned stretch of sea.
dam_waterproof: Keeping outside water from entering the joined hull.
dam_careen: Lay a ship over to expose and clean its underwater body.
dam_drift: Be carried by wind or water without making deliberate headway.
dam_reef: Gather a sail up rather than leaving it spread to the wind.
dam_swelltide: Incoming, rising water as distinct from a weather flood.
dam_sea_league: A league of distance at sea in the narrator’s reckoning; distinct from an alliance.
dam_crew: A member of the working complement of a vessel.
dam_bootyshare: The narrator’s share of the goods and captives divided among the company.
dam_gear: Put a vessel in suitable trim for sailing.
dam_daybreeze: The onshore wind from the sea described by the narrator.
dam_mainland: The continuous continental land, in contrast with adjacent islands.
dam_ammunition: Materials for loading the party's guns, kept as a travelling stock.
dam_tow: Move a vessel through water by pulling it along.
dam_backpack: A traveller's bag carried on the back.
dam_pistol_range: The ordinary reach of a pistol shot, used as a measure of proximity in the narrative.
dam_fisgig: A pronged fishing implement named alongside the lance and the harpoon.
dam_harpoon: A barbed implement for striking large aquatic animals, distinct from the pronged fish-gig.
dam_pecary: One of the two animals termed wild hogs by the narrator.
dam_warree: The second locally distinguished wild hog in Dampier's account; no modern species assignment.
dam_plantain: The banana-like tropical food plant. Distinct from the small medicinal herb of the same English name.
dam_yam: The edible tuber called yam, distinguished from the potato grown with it.
dam_potato: The crop the narrator calls potato; his term is retained without identifying the species.
dam_pineapple: The tropical crowned fruit from which the drink is made.
dam_pine_drink: The local drink made from pineapples as described by Dampier.
dam_superstition: The author's characterization of religious observances he looked for.
dam_plantation: An area planted for food by a household in this account.
dam_compass: Portable magnetic compass used in the overland march.
dam_hut: A small improvised shelter built during the march.
dam_calabash: A drinking vessel made of a gourd shell.
dam_hatchet: A small hand axe, repeatedly given in payment to guides.
dam_machete: The long knife offered in trade, called a macheat in the source.
dam_bamboo: A large jointed cane of which Dampier sealed a length to hold his journal.
dam_garrison: A settlement held by a military garrison.
dam_barbecue: Here a sleeping platform supported clear of the ground, not a cooked meal.
dam_berry: The local fruit Dampier calls macaw-berries; the species is not assumed.
dam_quaum: The large forest bird called a quaum by Dampier.
dam_barcolongo: The long vessel called a barco-longo, here used by a French privateer.
dam_ford: Go across a river on foot.
dam_bead: A small pierced ornament strung on cord and exchanged as a gift.
dam_eddy: A back-circling current near a riverbank.
dam_fertile: Rich soil capable of bearing plentiful crops.
dam_dollar: A silver dollar or piece of eight used in this voyage account.
dam_careless: Wanting ordinary care or attention, an omission rather than unconcern over danger.
dam_corn_ear: The fruit-bearing head of the corn plant, distinct from the bodily ear.
dam_settlement: An inhabited settlement or village in the region of the isthmus.
dam_shears: Small paired cutting blades given in trade.
